title: The Moon Smells Like Gunpowder
description:
Apollo astronauts said Moon dust smelled like spent gunpowder. Strangely, Moon samples back on Earth don't smell at all.

Sources: NASA Science, "The Mysterious Smell of Moondust" (2006); NASA on lunar dust and Harrison Schmitt's "lunar hay fever" (Apollo 17).
Narration is AI-generated text-to-speech and the pictures are AI-generated illustrations.

#shorts #moon #space #science

segments.text: Astronauts say the Moon smells like gunpowder.
segments.image: close-up of an Apollo-era astronaut helmet visor covered in grey lunar dust, harsh sunlight, black sky, lunar surface reflected in the gold visor

segments.text: After moonwalks, Apollo crews climbed back into the lander with their suits caked in Moon dust.
segments.image: cramped interior of a 1970s lunar module cabin, two astronauts in dusty white spacesuits with helmets off, grey dust on the floor and on their suits, dim instrument lights

segments.text: When they took off their helmets, it smelled like spent gunpowder. Crew after crew said the same thing.
segments.image: faint wisps of grey smoke drifting in the air like after a gunshot, dark moody background, soft rim light

segments.text: But Moon samples brought back to Earth smell of nothing. Scientists think the fresh dust reacted with the air in the cabin.
segments.image: a grey Moon rock sample sitting inside a stainless steel laboratory glovebox, gloved hands, clean white lab light

segments.text: And it is nasty stuff. With no wind or water to smooth it, each grain is jagged like broken glass. One astronaut even got lunar hay fever.
segments.say: And it is nasty stuff. With no wind or water to smooth it, each grain is jagged, like broken glass. One astronaut even got lunar hay fever.
segments.image: extreme macro of jagged sharp grey mineral grains like crushed glass, scanning electron microscope style lighting, black background

segments.text: The Moon smells like gunpowder. Unreal, but true. Subscribe.
